title: Prescriptions & Renewals: one open prescription per medication and strength, one controlled prescriber at a time
content:
**Medication Management Office standard — Prescriptions & Renewals.**

**1. The limit.** A patient holds at most the class's limit of open prescriptions of one medication and strength. A new prescription of a medication and strength is written only when the patient holds no other prescription of the same medication and strength in status prescribed, active, renewal requested or on hold.

**2. Evidence.** The condition is read from the prescription records before the new prescription is written: the patient, the medication as written, the strength and form as written, and the status of each prescription. The comparison is made on the same patient, the same medication and the same strength together.

**3. A change of dose or strength.** A dose or strength change is a new prescription that discontinues the old one with reason "replaced by new prescription"; where the class requires a visit for a dose change, the new prescription is written only after a visit.

**4. Controlled prescriptions across medications.** A patient may hold Schedule II Controlled Prescription and Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription prescriptions only from one prescribing clinician at a time: a controlled prescription from a second Linden Ridge prescriber is not written while another prescriber's controlled prescription is open, unless the first is discontinued with reason "transferred care".

**5. Status table for clause 1.** The statuses listed in clause 1 are the complete list that counts as open.

| Status of the existing prescription of the same medication and strength | Counts against clause 1 |
|---|---|
| prescribed | yes |
| active | yes |
| renewal requested | yes |
| on hold | yes |
| expired | no |
| discontinued | no |

**6. Cases (hypothetical).**
- An active prescription for "20 mg tablet" of a medication exists; a further prescription of the same medication as a "20 mg tablet" is not written.
- The only earlier prescription of that medication and strength expired last month; the expired prescription does not count, and clause 1 does not stop a new one.
- A patient holds an open Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription from one Linden Ridge prescriber; a Schedule II Controlled Prescription from a different Linden Ridge prescriber is not written while the first remains open, unless the first has been discontinued with reason "transferred care".
